from report import summarize


def test_summary_counts():
    """Verify summarize returns correct counts for each status category."""
    jobs = [
        {"status": "New", "id": 1},
        {"status": "new", "id": 2},
        {"status": "NEW ", "id": 3},
        {"status": "APPLIED", "id": 4},
        {"status": "applied", "id": 5},
        {"status": "applied ", "id": 6},
        {"status": "REJECTED", "id": 7},
        {"status": "rejected", "id": 8},
        {"status": "rejected ", "id": 9},
        {"status": None, "id": 10},
        {"status": "", "id": 11},
        {"status": "unknown", "id": 12},
        {"status": "OTHER", "id": 13},
        {"status": "Other", "id": 14},
        {"status": "OTHER ", "id": 15},
    ]
    result = summarize(jobs)
    # Verify all four keys exist in the expected order
    expected_keys = ["new", "applied", "rejected", "other"]
    assert list(result.keys()) == expected_keys, f"Keys mismatch: {result.keys()}"
    # Verify counts
    assert result["new"] == 4, f"Expected 4 'new', got {result['new']}"
    assert result["applied"] == 4, f"Expected 4 'applied', got {result['applied']}"
    assert result["rejected"] == 4, f"Expected 4 'rejected', got {result['rejected']}"
    assert result["other"] == 4, f"Expected 4 'other', got {result['other']}"
    # Verify input is unchanged
    status_values = [job["status"] for job in jobs]
    assert status_values == [
        "New",
        "new",
        "NEW ",
        "APPLIED",
        "applied",
        "applied ",
        "REJECTED",
        "rejected",
        "rejected ",
        None,
        "",
        "unknown",
        "OTHER",
        "Other",
        "OTHER ",
    ]


if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_summary_counts()
    print("All tests passed.")"}}}]
